clinician.final_diagnosis: Ramsay Hunt Syndrome Associated with Varicella-Zoster Virus Encephalitis
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 8-year-old boy presented with 3 days of fever, left ear pain, swelling, and vesicular rash around the left ear pinna. Initial exam revealed left ear swelling with vesicular lesions extending to the maxillary dermatome and tender cervical lymphadenopathy. On day 2, he developed lower motor neuron facial nerve palsy consistent with Ramsay Hunt syndrome. On day 3, he developed neurological signs including vomiting, dysarthria, unsteady gait, and drowsiness indicating encephalitis. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was performed and PCR confirmed varicella-zoster virus infection, confirming VZV encephalitis associated with Ramsay Hunt syndrome.
